exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. PyTorch stable documentation reviewed 2026-09-19 (current docs identified as 2.14).

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; typed recall and coding questions provide the scored retrieval signal.

authoring_notes: This is a practical learning track, not a certification. Domain weights are curriculum emphasis weights used for adaptive selection. Learning placeholders are exact cloze versions of their revealed text. Reviewed against PyTorch 2.14-era official documentation and the app's structured typed-fill code/table renderer on 2026-09-19.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` tells autograd to track operations needed to compute gradients with respect to that tensor in normal grad mode.

reveal.text: `requires_grad=True` tells autograd to track operations needed to compute gradients with respect to that tensor in normal grad mode.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Model Parameters __________ by default unless you explicitly freeze them.

reveal.text: Model Parameters require gradients by default unless you explicitly freeze them.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Setting `requires_grad` __________ backpropagation; gradients are populated after a backward computation.

reveal.text: Setting `requires_grad` does not itself run backpropagation; gradients are populated after a backward computation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` computes gradients through the recorded graph and accumulates them into `.grad` fields of relevant leaf tensors.

reveal.text: `loss.backward()` computes gradients through the recorded graph and accumulates them into `.grad` fields of relevant leaf tensors.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Call backward after computing the scalar loss and __________.

reveal.text: Call backward after computing the scalar loss and before the optimizer update.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Calling backward repeatedly without clearing parameter gradients __________ additional gradient values.

reveal.text: Calling backward repeatedly without clearing parameter gradients accumulates additional gradient values.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: PyTorch __________ parameter gradients by default, so each backward pass adds to existing `.grad` values.

reveal.text: PyTorch accumulates parameter gradients by default, so each backward pass adds to existing `.grad` values.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Clear gradients once per optimizer update unless you intentionally implement gradient accumulation over __________.

reveal.text: Clear gradients once per optimizer update unless you intentionally implement gradient accumulation over multiple microbatches.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Forgetting to clear gradients in a normal one-batch-per-step loop causes __________.

reveal.text: Forgetting to clear gradients in a normal one-batch-per-step loop causes unintended accumulation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` returns a tensor detached from the current autograd graph.

reveal.text: `tensor.detach()` returns a tensor detached from the current autograd graph.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use detaching when you need a value for logging or another computation that __________ through the original history.

reveal.text: Use detaching when you need a value for logging or another computation that should not backpropagate through the original history.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Detaching is different from copying; the detached tensor can __________ with the original tensor.

reveal.text: Detaching is different from copying; the detached tensor can share storage with the original tensor.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` clears or resets gradients associated with parameters managed by the optimizer.

reveal.text: `optimizer.zero_grad()` clears or resets gradients associated with parameters managed by the optimizer.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A common step is __________, run forward/loss, call backward, then call optimizer step.

reveal.text: A common step is zero gradients, run forward/loss, call backward, then call optimizer step.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Skipping gradient clearing in an ordinary loop makes gradients __________.

reveal.text: Skipping gradient clearing in an ordinary loop makes gradients accumulate across batches.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` updates parameters using the gradients currently stored for the optimizer-managed parameters.

reveal.text: `optimizer.step()` updates parameters using the gradients currently stored for the optimizer-managed parameters.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Call it __________ has produced gradients for the current update.

reveal.text: Call it after backward has produced gradients for the current update.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Calling `step()` __________ normally means the current batch gradients are not available for that update.

reveal.text: Calling `step()` before backward normally means the current batch gradients are not available for that update.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` converts a one-element tensor such as a scalar loss into a standard Python number.

reveal.text: `loss.item()` converts a one-element tensor such as a scalar loss into a standard Python number.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when you need a numeric loss value for simple __________ or aggregation outside tensor computation.

reveal.text: Use it when you need a numeric loss value for simple logging or aggregation outside tensor computation.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Calling `.item()` removes the value from tensor/autograd computation, so __________ the returned Python number to continue the differentiable loss calculation.

reveal.text: Calling `.item()` removes the value from tensor/autograd computation, so do not use the returned Python number to continue the differentiable loss calculation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` enables training behavior for mode-sensitive modules, while `model.eval()` switches them to evaluation behavior.

reveal.text: `model.train()` enables training behavior for mode-sensitive modules, while `model.eval()` switches them to evaluation behavior.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `train()` before training epochs and `__________` before validation or inference.

reveal.text: Use `train()` before training epochs and `eval()` before validation or inference.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `eval()` __________; pair it with no-grad or inference mode when gradient tracking is unnecessary.

reveal.text: `eval()` does not disable autograd; pair it with no-grad or inference mode when gradient tracking is unnecessary.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` disables recording operations for reverse-mode gradient calculation inside its context.

reveal.text: `torch.no_grad()` disables recording operations for reverse-mode gradient calculation inside its context.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for __________ when you do not need backward and may later reuse resulting tensors in normal grad mode.

reveal.text: Use it for validation or inference when you do not need backward and may later reuse resulting tensors in normal grad mode.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: No-grad mode is __________ `model.eval()`; one controls autograd recording and the other controls module training behavior.

reveal.text: No-grad mode is separate from `model.eval()`; one controls autograd recording and the other controls module training behavior.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` disables autograd recording and removes additional autograd-related overhead for computations that will not later participate in grad-mode graphs.

reveal.text: `torch.inference_mode()` disables autograd recording and removes additional autograd-related overhead for computations that will not later participate in grad-mode graphs.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for __________ paths when its stricter tensor-lifetime constraints fit your code.

reveal.text: Use it for pure inference paths when its stricter tensor-lifetime constraints fit your code.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Tensors created in inference mode __________ in computations that autograd needs to record.

reveal.text: Tensors created in inference mode cannot later be used in computations that autograd needs to record.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Setting a parameter or module to `__________` excludes those parameters from gradient computation in normal grad mode.

reveal.text: Setting a parameter or module to `requires_grad_(False)` excludes those parameters from gradient computation in normal grad mode.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Freezing a __________ is commonly done before training only a new head.

reveal.text: Freezing a pretrained backbone is commonly done before training only a new head.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Freezing gradients __________ Dropout or BatchNorm to evaluation mode.

reveal.text: Freezing gradients does not automatically switch Dropout or BatchNorm to evaluation mode.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `torch.nn.utils.__________` clips the total norm of parameter gradients in place to a specified maximum norm.

reveal.text: `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_` clips the total norm of parameter gradients in place to a specified maximum norm.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Apply gradient clipping __________ has produced gradients and before the optimizer step.

reveal.text: Apply gradient clipping after backward has produced gradients and before the optimizer step.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Clipping __________ has nothing useful to clip for the current batch.

reveal.text: Clipping before backward has nothing useful to clip for the current batch.
